meta_description: A Nintendo Switch homebrew that browses your own library server and installs your backups and homebrew from it over HTTPS: a catalogue with names and icons, a download queue that pauses and resumes, nothing stored in the clear.
hero_title: Your game library, on the console
hero_sub: HTTPS everywhere · Pause and resume · Nothing stored in the clear
hero_text: PlayShelf browses a library server you run yourself (AeroFoil, Ownfoil or a plain JSON index) and installs your own backups and homebrew from it: NSP, NSZ, XCI and XCZ, queued, paused, resumed, checked as they install.
no_release: No release yet: PlayShelf is in development, and the simulator shows where it stands.
own_text: PlayShelf installs what you own, from a server you run. It does not read encrypted Tinfoil indexes, does not send Tinfoil's authentication headers, and will not support any service that distributes games without the rights to do so.
f_catalogue_text: Every game as a cover with its size and add-ons, searched, sorted and in sections; a game's page installs its base game, its updates and add-ons, or “{{app:library/install_all}}” at once.
f_downloads_text: A queue installed one package after the other, paused and resumed, tried again by itself from where it stopped; up to 8 connections per download, and the next packages fetched ahead.
f_security_text: HTTPS only, certificates always verified; a server of your network with a certificate of its own trusted once you have compared its key; passwords sealed for the console.
f_lan_text: “{{app:library/discover}}” lists the AeroFoil and Ownfoil servers of your network; a server can have an address at home and one over the Internet.
f_titles_text: A title database on the SD card, from CyberFoil-DB, NXMeta and Ghostland or your own sources, each pack checked by its SHA-256.
f_library_text: The Library shows what the console has, and what the server has newer: an update to install, the add-ons still missing.
f_updates_text: A new release installed from the app, in place, with sphaira or the Homebrew App Store, and the previous one kept to go back to.
f_languages_text: The 15 languages of the console, light and dark themes, larger text on the TV.
shot_catalogue_alt: Catalogue: the demo server's games as covers, with their size and add-ons, under the server, the search and the order
shot_game_sheet_alt: A game's page: Install everything, then its base game and its update, each with its size
shot_downloads_alt: Downloads: a game installed, its two packages done, then the downloads' settings
shot_library_alt: Library: the game installed on the console, with its version
shot_preferences_alt: Preferences: the language, the theme, the text size, the tab PlayShelf opens on, then updates and the title database
simulator_title: Try it before you install it
simulator_text: The real PlayShelf runs in your browser, against a simulated console and a demo library server of made-up games: browse the catalogue, install a game, pause a download, try every setting.
install_1: A Nintendo Switch with Atmosphère, and sys-patch or sigpatches.
install_2: Extract playshelf.zip from the latest release to the root of the SD card.
install_3: Launch PlayShelf from the homebrew menu.
start_1: “{{app:library/add_server}}”: its https:// address, on your network or over the Internet, and its account if it has one; or “{{app:library/discover}}”.
start_2: In the “{{app:tabs/catalogue}}”, a game's page: “{{app:library/install_all}}”, or a package of it.
start_3: The “{{app:tabs/downloads}}” install them one after the other; the “{{app:tabs/library}}” shows them once installed.
faq_what_a: A server you run on a computer or a NAS, which lists your backups and serves them: AeroFoil or Ownfoil, or any web server with a plain JSON index of your files. PlayShelf reads its catalogue and downloads the packages from it.
faq_own_q: Where do the games come from?
faq_own_a: From your own server only: PlayShelf comes with no game and no source of games. It is made to install your own backups and homebrew.
faq_servers_q: Which servers does it work with?
faq_servers_a: AeroFoil and Ownfoil, through their API, and any server that serves a JSON index of files (files, directories, titledb), over HTTPS. A user name and password if the server asks for them.
faq_tinfoil_a: Not encrypted ones: PlayShelf reads no encrypted index, sends no Tinfoil authentication header and no console identifier. A plain JSON index works.
faq_https_a: So that the catalogue, your password and the packages cannot be read or changed on the way. A server of your network with a certificate of its own is trusted once, after you have compared its key; there is no option to turn the checks off.
faq_cfw_a: Atmosphère, and sys-patch or sigpatches for the games to start: PlayShelf says so before installing when it finds neither.
faq_switch2_q: Does it work on a Switch 2?
faq_switch2_a: No: there is no Atmosphère for the Switch 2.
faq_free_a: Yes: free and open-source software, under the GNU GPL v3.
